Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are close to finalizing the procurement package but have a few precise metering questions that the finance and engineering teams flagged — they want the baseline (hosted API) pricing to be crystal clear before we sign. Attached is a short RFP appendix with example call patterns. Key asks: 1) For billing, how are system prompts vs. user prompts counted (input vs output)? 2) If we make streaming responses and call an external tool (e.g., a retrieval API) in the middle of a completion, how are those tool-related tokens attributable (do they go to input or output buckets)? 3) Do you round per-request, per-response chunk, or per-token? We have strict forecasting requirements so even small rounding rules move the math.

Can you confirm exact rules and provide a sample invoice line item for a typical daily workload (100k user-input tokens, 300k model-output tokens, ~5% tooloutput by token)? Also, please attach the current ratecard PDF and any example invoices you can share.

Appreciate it — Samantha

Samantha — thanks for the clear note. I pulled together the billing rules and a simple worked example below; attaching the current ratecard as requested. High level summary up front:

- System prompts (model/system role) are counted as input tokens.
- User prompts and any prefix/context are input tokens.
- Model-generated text is output tokens.
- Tool calls: the text sent into a tool as part of the request (tool input) is treated as input tokens; tokens returned by the tool (tool output) are treated as output tokens unless the tool output is directly re-ingested as model input in the same API operation (in which case you'll see both counts across requests).
- Rounding: we count raw token totals per request and bill the exact total (no additional bucket rounding per 100 tokens). For streaming, we do not artificially add tokens because of chunking; billed tokens are the canonical tokenizer counts for the final pieces (we reconcile after the call).

Worked example (daily):
- User input tokens: 100,000
- Model output tokens: 300,000
- Tool outputs included in responses (~5% of output): 15,000 tool-output tokens (counted as output)
- System prompt context (shared templates, per-request addition): 10,000 (input)

Net billed tokens for the day: input = 110,000; output = 315,000.

I'll attach a sample invoice line that maps to the hosted API rate bands. If you want we can also provide a CSV export with per-endpoint, per-route breakout for your forecasting system.

Attachment: Redwood_Ratecard_v1.pdf

—Karthik

Thanks — couple of follow-ups from engineering: 1) If a streaming completion emits partial tokens across multiple network frames, you said Redwood reconciles on the tokenizer canonical counts post-call. Do you sometimes see off-by-one when tooling calls inject whitespace/markup? 2) For toolcalls: suppose the model emits a tool call that returns 2,400 tokens and then the model consumes that tool output to produce another 1,000 tokens in the same logical flow; how will that be surfaced on the invoice?

We want to be confident that we can predict upstream egress costs (we do some chargeback) and also prove to our auditors that the counting rules are deterministic.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Baseline question on token counting and final rate

Samantha — great questions. Final clarifications and what you'll see on invoice/CSV exports: 

1) Streaming/chunking: billing uses tokenizer-level counts computed from the canonical post-processed strings. Network frames that split tokens do not create extra charges. In practice we tokenize the reconstructed output; if a tool injects markup/whitespace that is returned as content, those characters are tokenized like any other text — there is no special-case rounding that adds extra tokens. Edge-case off-by-one only happens if the same logical text is sent twice in two distinct API requests (that would be billed twice).

2) Tool call flows: bills are request-centric. Example flow you described:
- Request A: model emits tool call; tool returns 2,400 tokens (tool-output). That 2,400 is counted as output for Request A.
- If Request A then immediately posts a new Request B that includes that tool output as model input and the model generates another 1,000 tokens, Request B will show those 2,400 as input (since included in the request payload) and the 1,000 as output. The invoice/CSV will reflect both requests separately. Aggregates: input += 2,400; output += 1,000 (in addition to the original billed 2,400 output on Request A). This is transparent in the per-request CSV export we can share.

3) Rounding/aggregation: we aggregate raw tokenizer counts across the billing window and bill the summed integers. We do not round up to fixed buckets (e.g., 100-token buckets). We do not add hidden per-request buffer tokens.

Next steps: I'll generate a sample CSV export for your RFP example and a modeled invoice for the committed 1.2M monthly tier with proration for a 12/15 start date. Expect those artifacts in a follow-up within 24 hours.

—Karthik
